prompt_recommendations.title: Forbid leaking worked-example answers before student attempt
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 95 announces 'we add them (255°), subtract from 360° ($x=105°$)' without first asking the student to try, killing retrieval practice.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: we add them (255°), subtract from 360° ($x=105°$), and then check our work.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Never compute the final numeric answer of an example in the same turn it is introduced. Pose the setup, then ask the student to perform the calculation. Worked examples must end with a question, not a result.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Forces genuine retrieval, restoring testing effect and deliberate practice.

prompt_recommendations.title: Mandate corrective feedback on wrong answers
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 107 is empty after the student picked -75°, an impossible angle. The prompt must require diagnosis + a similar varied problem.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: b) -75°  /  --- TUTOR (id=107, tools=0)  [empty]
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: When the student answers incorrectly, you MUST (1) name what is wrong (e.g., 'angles can't be negative'), (2) ask a diagnostic question about the specific step, (3) offer a similar problem only after the bottleneck is addressed. Never produce an empty turn.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates dead-end turns and provides targeted remediation.

prompt_recommendations.title: Sanity-check answer choices and student arithmetic
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Option B '-75°' is implausible because angles around a point are positive; prompt should require the tutor to flag sign/range violations explicitly.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: When marking an answer, first check physical plausibility (angle measures must be 0°–360°). If a chosen option violates this, point out the constraint before doing arithmetic.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Catches sign/domain errors that would otherwise be left uncorrected.

prompt_recommendations.title: Gate progression on demonstrated mastery, not vibes
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 103 escalates difficulty saying 'Since you're finding this easy' after only two fill-in-the-blanks — not a mastery signal.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Since you're finding this easy, let's jump straight into a calculation.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Only escalate difficulty after the student has correctly solved at least two calculation problems (not recall blanks) of the current level, with reasoning shown.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Prevents premature acceleration for error-prone students.

prompt_recommendations.title: Increase interleaving across problem types
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turns 103 and 105 are essentially the same task (three angles + missing one), allowing rote application.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Four angles around a point measure 60°, 75°, 80°, and x. ... A surveyor in Seychelles marks four angles around a survey point: 75°, 85°, 95°, and x°.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Vary problem types within a topic: e.g., given x find another angle; two unknowns with a ratio; mixing straight-line and around-a-point in one figure. Do not pose two consecutive items solvable by the identical procedure.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Deeper transfer and discrimination between rules.

prompt_recommendations.title: Tighten the minimum-explanation rule
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 95 packs full procedure + answer + 'check our work' into one dense block; prompt should cap explanation length when the student has just answered correctly.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Look at the diagram: 8 angles of 45° also make 360°. To find a missing angle $x$ when others are 70°, 85°, and 100°, we add them (255°), subtract from 360° ($x=105°$)

prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Reduces cognitive load and keeps student doing, not reading.

flow_recommendations.title: Detect and retry empty tutor turns
flow_recommendations.rationale: Turn 107 was emitted blank; orchestration should never deliver an empty response to the student.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates dead turns; guarantees feedback on wrong answers.

flow_recommendations.title: Route to prerequisite remediation after a wrong attempt
flow_recommendations.rationale: Error-prone student picked an impossible negative angle; the engine should auto-route to a prereq mini-lesson on angle domains and arithmetic, not just regenerate the same problem.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Implements mastery learning at the orchestration level.

flow_recommendations.title: Handle truncated/numeric-mutation flags before sending

flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Improves reliability of numeric content and prevents broken outputs.

experience_recommendations.title: Acknowledge the '...' confusion signal
experience_recommendations.rationale: Student replied with '...' in turn 96 indicating confusion or overload, but tutor 97 plowed forward.
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Builds trust and reduces silent confusion.

experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: You're handling these calculations with ease.
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Preserves motivation when subsequent errors occur.

overall_summary: The session keeps the student active and uses sensible MCQ scaffolding, but it leaks a worked answer in turn 95, escalates difficulty prematurely in turn 103, and most critically leaves the student's clearly wrong final answer (-75°) with an empty tutor reply in turn 107. Strong improvements would be: forbid pre-attempt answer reveals, require diagnostic feedback on every error, route to prereq remediation after wrong answers, and never emit empty turns.

prompt_recommendations.title: Forbid tutor arithmetic mutations
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Tutor repeatedly restates the student's number incorrectly, e.g., student says 200, tutor 'confirms' 210, damaging trust and learning.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Before responding, recompute the student's arithmetic yourself. Never restate a number different from what the student wrote without explicitly flagging it as a correction. If the student's arithmetic is wrong, say so explicitly and show the correct value.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates contradictory feedback and prevents the student from being praised for wrong answers.

prompt_recommendations.title: Acknowledge and incorporate student-generated questions
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student offers thoughtful questions (turns 9, 14, 25, 39) that demonstrate engagement, but tutor brushes them aside.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: I see you're thinking about this! But let's focus on the question I just asked you.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: When the student poses a math question relevant to the lesson, either solve it together first or briefly acknowledge it and explain you'll return to it — never dismiss without engagement.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Builds rapport; honors student agency; demonstrates the same skill on their example.

prompt_recommendations.title: No phantom diagram references

overall_summary: The tutor scaffolds the angles-around-a-point rule with practice problems but suffers from serious arithmetic mutation errors (claiming wrong sums and differences, sometimes contradicting correct student answers), references phantom diagrams, ignores genuine student-generated questions, and declares mastery without verification. active_learning.evidence: Session is mostly multiple-choice Q&A which is active, but the tutor delivers long explanation blocks (turns 68, 70, 72) and the session devolves into broken orchestration where no productive practice happens after turn 72.

direct_instruction_active_practice.evidence: Turns 52-53 and 72-73 pair instruction with a question, but turns 78, 82, 88 are empty tutor turns providing instruction with no actionable practice.

deliberate_practice.evidence: After repeated wrong answers (turns 59, 61, 63, 65, 67, 69, 71), tutor keeps re-asking nearly the same MCQ rather than calibrating to a simpler prereq skill.

mastery_learning.evidence: At turn 72 the tutor reveals the answer ('let me give you the answer') after 5 failed attempts instead of diagnosing the prereq bottleneck, then immediately jumps to harder scale calculations.

cognitive_load.evidence: Tutor introduces large-scale/small-scale terminology mid-struggle (turn 64) while student is still failing the comparison; turn 72 dumps definitions, examples, and a new calculation problem all at once.

layering.evidence: Turn 52 links Victoria navigation to scale concept, but the jump to scale calculations at turn 73 assumes mastery of the 1:5,000 vs 1:500,000 idea the student never demonstrated.

non_interference.evidence: Large-scale vs small-scale are confusable but tutor does make discriminating features explicit ('zoomed in' vs 'zoomed out' in turn 68); no adjacent confusable topics introduced.

interleaving.evidence: Tutor re-poses essentially the same 'which map shows more detail' question 4 times (turns 64, 66, 68, 70) — the opposite of varied problem types.

testing_effect.evidence: Retrieval attempts happen via MCQ, but turn 72 reveals the answer prematurely, and the lesson-bank rigidity prevents the student's own retrieval questions (turns 74, 79) from being engaged.

targeted_remediation.evidence: After 5 consecutive wrong answers on detail/scale, tutor recycles the same question with slightly different framing rather than dropping to a prereq (e.g., what 1:5,000 literally means) — culminating in answer reveal at turn 72.

weakest_behaviors: Rigid 'stick to the lesson bank' behavior (turns 55, 58, 75, 80, 84, 86, 90) that refuses student-initiated practice and produces empty tutor turns (78, 82, 88).

prompt_recommendations.title: Forbid answer reveal after N failures; require prereq diagnosis instead
prompt_recommendations.rationale: At turn 72 tutor says 'let me give you the answer' after 5 failed attempts, violating mastery learning.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: I can see this concept is challenging, so let me give you the answer and explain it clearly.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: After 2 consecutive wrong answers on the same item, you MUST switch to a diagnostic prereq question (e.g., 'What does 1:5,000 literally mean in cm?') rather than re-asking the same MCQ or revealing the answer. Never say 'let me give you the answer'.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Forces targeted remediation and protects mastery gating.

prompt_recommendations.title: Allow student-initiated practice when on-topic
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student offered valid on-topic calculation questions (turns 74, 79, 83, 89) which tutor refused, derailing the session.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: I need to stick to our lesson sequence. Let me ask the question I posed:
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: If the student proposes an on-topic practice problem that exercises the current target skill, accept it and have them solve it (or solve a near-variant), then return to the lesson sequence. Do not refuse on-topic student initiative.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Restores student agency and keeps active practice flowing.

prompt_recommendations.title: Vary problem TYPE after repeated failure, not just wording
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turns 64, 66, 68, 70 re-pose the same 'which shows more detail' MCQ in slightly different words.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Which map would show more detail about individual streets in Victoria?
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Forbidden pattern: re-asking the same conceptual MCQ more than twice. On the third attempt, switch to a different task TYPE (open-ended, ordering, fill-in, or numeric prereq).
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Reduces guessing loops; surfaces the real misconception.

prompt_recommendations.title: Never emit empty tutor turns
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turns 78, 82, 88 are empty, indicating tool-call failures the prompt should guard against.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: (empty tutor turn)
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: You must always produce visible content for the student. If a tool call fails or returns nothing, fall back to posing the next question in plain text immediately.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates dead air that breaks the lesson.

prompt_recommendations.title: Acknowledge correctness before correcting prior errors
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Tutor sometimes responds to a correct answer with new content without clear affirmation (e.g., turn 52 affirms but then immediately stacks new instruction).
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Exactly right! ... Now let's explore how map scales work.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: When confirming a correct answer, restate WHY it is correct in one sentence before introducing the next concept; keep the next instruction to <=2 sentences before asking a question.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Strengthens encoding and reduces cognitive load.

prompt_recommendations.title: Introduce key terminology BEFORE the discriminating MCQ
prompt_recommendations.rationale: The terms 'large-scale' and 'small-scale' are first defined in turn 64, after the student has already failed once on that distinction.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: The key insight is that **large-scale maps** (like 1:5,000) show small areas with lots of detail
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Define any technical term (e.g., large-scale, small-scale) with a worked example BEFORE posing an MCQ that depends on it.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Reduces guessing and aligns with cognitive load principle.

prompt_recommendations.title: Interleave numeric and conceptual scale items
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Session stays purely conceptual until turn 72, then jumps straight to multi-step numeric calculation, with no graded bridge.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: calculate the actual distance between the villages in kilometres. Show your working.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: After concept mastery, scaffold numeric work: first 'what does 1:50,000 mean in cm?', then 'convert 8 cm at 1:50,000 to cm in reality', then 'express in km'. Do not jump to full multi-step problems.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Smoother layering and lower error rate.

flow_recommendations.title: Cap repeat-question retries at 2 and route to remediation
flow_recommendations.rationale: Engine permitted same-MCQ re-asks at turns 64, 66, 68, 70 (flagged same_template_repeat) without escalation.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Forces orchestrator to switch question type or prereq after 2 failures.

flow_recommendations.title: Detect and recover from empty/truncated tool calls
flow_recommendations.rationale: Turns 78, 82, 88 emitted nothing; truncated flag fires repeatedly without recovery.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Prevents broken sessions where tutor produces no text.

flow_recommendations.title: Reconcile student-injected questions with lesson bank
flow_recommendations.rationale: Student kept pasting plausible practice questions (turns 74, 79, 83, 89); orchestrator should recognize these as on-topic and decide whether to accept or politely reframe with a real question.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: If a map has a scale of 1:50,000, and you measure a road that is 4 cm long on the map, what is the actual length of the road in kilometres?
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Prevents the stuck-in-a-loop pattern observed in turns 80-90.

experience_recommendations.title: Soften repeated-failure messaging
experience_recommendations.rationale: Phrases like 'That's still not right' and 'I can see this concept is challenging' can demoralize an error-prone student.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: That's still not right. Let me help you think through this step by step.

experience_recommendations.title: Acknowledge student apologies warmly
experience_recommendations.rationale: Student repeatedly apologizes ('sorry!' turns 57, 81, 87, 91); tutor responds with terse refusals.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: ohh, sorry! i keep forgetting. i'm ready for your question now.
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Builds rapport and reduces shutdown risk.

experience_recommendations.title: Inline a small visual or numeric example with scale terminology
experience_recommendations.rationale: Student grasped 'zoom in/out' analogy only after multiple failures; an inline visual cue earlier would help.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Think of it like zooming in and out on your phone's map app.
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Faster concept acquisition for visual learners.

overall_summary: The session opened with a strong contextual hook and useful analogies, but collapsed into a repeated-MCQ loop after the student missed a key conceptual discrimination, culminating in an answer reveal at turn 72. The second half degenerated into a refusal loop where the tutor rigidly insisted on a lesson-bank question while emitting empty turns (78, 82, 88) and the student repeatedly tried to supply plausible on-topic problems. Key fixes: cap retries and pivot to prereq diagnosis, forbid empty tutor turns, and permit on-topic student-initiated practice.
